title: SEPE-SQED: Symbolic Quick Error Detection by Semantically Equivalent Program Execution
problem: SQED (Symbolic Quick Error Detection) relies on self-consistency checking but cannot detect single-instruction bugs where the instruction itself is faulty. This leaves instruction-level bugs undetected in formal chip verification.
motivation: Single-instruction bugs in hardware designs can cause critical failures, and current SQED methods lack mechanisms to detect them, requiring improved verification techniques.
method: SEPE-SQED uses program synthesis to generate instruction sequences with equivalent semantics to original instructions, then detects single-instruction bugs by comparing behavioral differences between original and equivalent sequences. A CEGIS framework with highest-priority-first algorithm efficiently manages the synthesis search space. By identifying where original and equivalent programs diverge, instruction-level faults are revealed.
key_novelty: Using semantically-equivalent program synthesis to extend bug detection beyond self-consistency checks, enabling identification of single-instruction faults through behavioral differentiation.
contributions: SEPE-SQED method that detects single-instruction bugs via semantic program equivalence
CEGIS-based algorithm with highest-priority-first strategy for efficient synthesis
50% improvement in generation speed for equivalent instruction sequences
Shorter execution traces for bug triggering compared to existing approaches

metrics.other: shorter trace length for bug detection

limitations: Scalability to large-scale chip designs and computational complexity bounds of the synthesis approach are not discussed.
primary_theme: formal verification through semantic program synthesis
